abihail_30.name: Abihail
abihail_30.who: A man of the tribe of Gad, son of Huri, whose seven sons headed Gadite families in Gilead and Bashan.
key: Abihail son of Huri is traced back through Jaroah, Gilead, and Michael in Gad's genealogy (1 Chronicles 5).
His sons Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jacan, Zia, and Eber headed their fathers' houses (1 Chronicles 5).
These Gadites were recorded in the days of Jotham of Judah and Jeroboam of Israel (1 Chronicles 5).

achaicus_60.name: Achaicus
achaicus_60.who: A believer from Corinth who, with Stephanas and Fortunatus, visited Paul and refreshed his spirit.
key: Paul rejoiced at the coming of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus from the Corinthian church (1 Corinthians 16).
They made up for the Corinthians' absence and refreshed Paul's spirit (1 Corinthians 16).
Paul urged the church to give recognition to such men (1 Corinthians 16).

alexander_187.name: Alexander
alexander_187.who: A member of the high-priestly family who sat with the council that questioned Peter and John.
key: The day after Peter and John's arrest, rulers, elders, and scribes gathered in Jerusalem (Acts 4).
Alexander was there with Annas, Caiaphas, and John, all of the high-priestly family (Acts 4).
The council asked by what power or name the apostles had healed the lame man (Acts 4).
Unable to deny the miracle, they warned the apostles not to speak in Jesus' name (Acts 4).

ananias_260.name: Ananias
ananias_260.who: The high priest who ordered Paul struck before the council and later accused him before Governor Felix.
key: When Paul spoke before the council, Ananias commanded those near him to strike Paul on the mouth (Acts 23).
Paul answered that God would strike him, calling him a whitewashed wall (Acts 23).
Five days after Paul reached Caesarea, Ananias came down with elders and the lawyer Tertullus (Acts 24).
They laid their charges against Paul before Governor Felix (Acts 24).

aner_266.name: Aner
aner_266.who: An Amorite near Hebron, brother of Mamre and Eshcol, who was allied with Abram.
key: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre the Amorite were allies of Abram, who lived by the oaks of Mamre (Genesis 14).
They went with Abram when he pursued the kings who had captured Lot (Genesis 14).
Abram refused the king of Sodom's goods but let Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre take their share (Genesis 14).

baanah_583.name: Baanah
baanah_583.who: A man of Netophah whose son Heleb was one of David's thirty mighty men.
key: Heleb son of Baanah of Netophah is listed among David's thirty mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
Chronicles names the son Heled son of Baanah of Netophah among David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 11).

chemosh_931.name: Chemosh
chemosh_931.who: The national god of Moab, for whom King Solomon built a high place east of Jerusalem.
key: An ancient song declared Moab undone, calling its people the people of Chemosh (Numbers 21).
Jephthah told the Ammonite king to keep what his god Chemosh had given him (Judges 11).
Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, east of Jerusalem (1 Kings 11).
Josiah defiled the high places Solomon had built for Chemosh and other gods (2 Kings 23).
Jeremiah foretold that Chemosh would go into exile and Moab would be ashamed of him (Jeremiah 48).
chemosh_931.label: False god

dagon_969.name: Dagon
dagon_969.who: A god of the Philistines, whose image fell broken before the ark of the LORD in Ashdod.
key: The Philistine lords gathered to sacrifice to Dagon, crediting him with Samson's capture (Judges 16).
Samson pulled down the house of Dagon, dying with the Philistines inside (Judges 16).
The captured ark was set beside Dagon in Ashdod, and Dagon fell face down before it (1 Samuel 5).
The next morning Dagon lay fallen again, his head and hands broken off on the threshold (1 Samuel 5).
The Philistines fastened Saul's head in the temple of Dagon (1 Chronicles 10).
dagon_969.label: False god

damaris_972.name: Damaris
damaris_972.who: A woman in Athens who believed after hearing Paul's address at the Areopagus.
key: Paul addressed the Areopagus in Athens, proclaiming the Creator who raised Jesus from the dead (Acts 17).
Some mocked, but some men joined Paul and believed (Acts 17).
Among those who believed were Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman named Damaris (Acts 17).

dishon_1016.name: Dishon
dishon_1016.who: A son of Seir the Horite and a chief among the Horites who lived in Seir before Esau's descendants.
key: Dishon was one of the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land (Genesis 36).
His sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran (Genesis 36).
He is listed among the chiefs of the Horites in the land of Seir (Genesis 36).
Chronicles repeats his name among the sons of Seir (1 Chronicles 1).

eker_1041.name: Eker
eker_1041.who: A man of Judah, son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, named in Chronicles' genealogy of Judah.
key: Eker was a son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers were Maaz and Jamin (1 Chronicles 2).

elah_1047.name: Elah
elah_1047.who: A son of Caleb son of Jephunneh and father of Kenaz, named in the genealogy of Judah.
key: Caleb son of Jephunneh had three sons: Iru, Elah, and Naam (1 Chronicles 4).
The son of Elah was Kenaz (1 Chronicles 4).

eliezer_1114.name: Eliezer
eliezer_1114.who: The second son of Moses and Zipporah, whose descendants served among the Levites over the temple treasuries.
key: Jethro brought Zipporah and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer, to Moses in the wilderness (Exodus 18).
Moses named him Eliezer, saying the God of his father had been his help (Exodus 18).
Eliezer had only one son, Rehabiah, whose descendants were very many (1 Chronicles 23).
His descendant Shelomoth oversaw the treasuries of gifts dedicated by David and his commanders (1 Chronicles 26).

gemariah_1296.name: Gemariah
gemariah_1296.who: A son of Shaphan the secretary, an official in whose chamber Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll.
key: Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll to the people from the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan (Jeremiah 36).
Gemariah's son Micaiah heard the words and reported them to the officials (Jeremiah 36).
Gemariah sat with the officials when Baruch read the scroll to them (Jeremiah 36).
He urged King Jehoiakim not to burn the scroll, but the king would not listen (Jeremiah 36).

hillel_1530.name: Hillel
hillel_1530.who: A man of Pirathon in Ephraim, father of Abdon, who judged Israel eight years.
key: Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel after Elon (Judges 12).
Abdon had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy donkeys (Judges 12).
Abdon son of Hillel died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim (Judges 12).

irad_611.name: Irad
irad_611.who: A descendant of Cain, son of Enoch and father of Mehujael.
key: Irad was born to Enoch, the son of Cain after whom Cain named his city (Genesis 4).
Irad fathered Mehujael, continuing Cain's line toward Lamech (Genesis 4).

ishmael_633.name: Ishmael
ishmael_633.who: The father of Zebadiah, governor of the house of Judah under King Jehoshaphat.
key: Jehoshaphat set Zebadiah son of Ishmael over all the king's matters (2 Chronicles 19).
Zebadiah served as governor of the house of Judah beside Amariah the chief priest (2 Chronicles 19).

jaazaniah_668.name: Jaazaniah
jaazaniah_668.who: A Rechabite, son of Jeremiah, whose family kept their ancestor's command to drink no wine.
key: Jeremiah brought Jaazaniah and the whole house of the Rechabites into a temple chamber (Jeremiah 35).
Offered wine, they refused, citing the command of their ancestor Jonadab son of Rechab (Jeremiah 35).
The LORD contrasted their obedience with Judah's refusal to listen to him (Jeremiah 35).
He promised that Jonadab would never lack a man to stand before him (Jeremiah 35).

jabal_673.name: Jabal
jabal_673.who: A son of Lamech and Adah, the father of those who live in tents and keep livestock.
key: Adah bore Jabal to Lamech, a descendant of Cain (Genesis 4).
He was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock (Genesis 4).
His brother Jubal was the father of those who play the lyre and pipe (Genesis 4).

jubal_1748.name: Jubal
jubal_1748.who: A son of Lamech and Adah, the father of all who play the lyre and pipe.
key: Adah bore Jubal to Lamech, a descendant of Cain (Genesis 4).
He was the father of all those who play the lyre and pipe (Genesis 4).
His brother Jabal was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock (Genesis 4).

jekuthiel_836.name: Jekuthiel
jekuthiel_836.who: A man of Judah, listed in Chronicles as the father, likely the founder, of the town of Zanoah.
key: Chronicles names Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel as sons borne by a Judahite wife (1 Chronicles 4).
Jekuthiel is called the father of Zanoah, a town of Judah (1 Chronicles 4).

jeroham_877.name: Jeroham
jeroham_877.who: A priest, father of Adaiah, whose family line traced back through Pashhur to Malchijah.
key: Adaiah son of Jeroham, of Pashhur's line, lived in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9).
Nehemiah gives his line as Jeroham son of Pelaliah, descended from Pashhur and Malchijah (Nehemiah 11).

joed_1646.name: Joed
joed_1646.who: A Benjaminite, son of Pedaiah and father of Meshullam, in the ancestry of Sallu of Jerusalem.
key: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, settled in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11).
Joed's line is traced back through Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah (Nehemiah 11).

kolaiah_1792.name: Kolaiah
kolaiah_1792.who: The father of Ahab, a false prophet among the exiles in Babylon whom Jeremiah condemned.
key: The LORD said Ahab son of Kolaiah was prophesying a lie in his name (Jeremiah 29).
He foretold that Nebuchadnezzar would kill Ahab and Zedekiah before the exiles' eyes (Jeremiah 29).
Their death by fire at the Babylonian king's hand would become a curse among the exiles (Jeremiah 29).

maaz_1872.name: Maaz
maaz_1872.who: A man of Judah, son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, named in Chronicles' genealogy of Judah.
key: Maaz was a son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel (1 Chronicles 2).
His brothers were Jamin and Eker (1 Chronicles 2).

moza_2113.name: Moza
moza_2113.who: A man of Judah, son of Caleb by his concubine Ephah, named in Judah's genealogy.
key: Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).
His father Caleb was the brother of Jerahmeel, both sons of Hezron (1 Chronicles 2).

ophrah_2254.name: Ophrah
ophrah_2254.who: A man of Judah, son of Meonothai, in the family line of Othniel, Israel's first judge.
key: Meonothai, of Othniel's family, fathered Ophrah (1 Chronicles 4).
Ophrah is listed among the descendants of Kenaz, the father of Othniel (1 Chronicles 4).

pasach_2279.name: Pasach
pasach_2279.who: A man of Asher, son of Japhlet, listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.
key: The sons of Japhlet were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath (1 Chronicles 7).
Japhlet was a son of Heber, the son of Asher's son Beriah (1 Chronicles 7).
Asher's descendants were remembered as choice mighty warriors and chiefs (1 Chronicles 7).

pethuel_2323.name: Pethuel
pethuel_2323.who: The father of Joel, the prophet who called Judah to repent after a locust plague.
key: The word of the LORD came to Joel son of Pethuel (Joel 1).
His son Joel described a devastating locust plague and called Judah to lament (Joel 1).

puah_2373.name: Puah
puah_2373.who: A man of Issachar, son of Dodo and father of Tola, who judged Israel after Abimelech.
key: Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel (Judges 10).
His son lived at Shamir in Ephraim's hill country and judged Israel twenty-three years (Judges 10).

sopater_2770.name: Sopater
sopater_2770.who: A believer from Berea, son of Pyrrhus, who accompanied Paul as he left Greece for Jerusalem.
key: Sopater of Berea, son of Pyrrhus, accompanied Paul as he returned through Macedonia (Acts 20).
His companions included Aristarchus, Secundus, Gaius of Derbe, Timothy, Tychicus, and Trophimus (Acts 20).
Sosipater, a relative of Paul who sent greetings to Rome, may be the same man (Romans 16).

tanhumeth_2824.name: Tanhumeth
tanhumeth_2824.who: The father of Seraiah, an army captain of Judah who came to Governor Gedaliah at Mizpah.
key: Seraiah son of Tanhumeth was among the captains who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah (2 Kings 25).
Gedaliah swore to these captains that serving the king of Babylon would go well with them (Jeremiah 40).

timaeus_2858.name: Timaeus
timaeus_2858.who: The father of Bartimaeus, the blind beggar whom Jesus healed near Jericho.
key: Bartimaeus, son of Timaeus, sat begging by the road as Jesus left Jericho (Mark 10).
Jesus restored his son's sight, and Bartimaeus followed him on the way (Mark 10).

uriel_2900.name: Uriel
uriel_2900.who: A Kohathite Levite, son of Tahath, named in Chronicles' genealogy of Kohath's descendants.
key: Chronicles lists Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul in succession among Kohath's descendants (1 Chronicles 6).
Heman's ancestry in the same chapter names Zephaniah son of Tahath at this point instead (1 Chronicles 6).

zillah_3080.name: Zillah
zillah_3080.who: One of the two wives of Lamech, Cain's descendant, and mother of Tubal-cain and Naamah.
key: Lamech took two wives, Adah and Zillah (Genesis 4).
Zillah bore Tubal-cain, a forger of bronze and iron tools, and his sister Naamah (Genesis 4).
Lamech addressed his boastful song of vengeance to Adah and Zillah (Genesis 4).
